newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy rate cut seen still a few weeks off.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy rate cut seen still a few weeks off.

text.p: A sharp brake in Italian inflation last month is spurring speculation the Bank of Italy might lower interest rates soon, but economists say an easing is probably still a few weeks off.
Statistics institute Istat said April's year on year consumer prices index stood at 1.7 percent, a steep tail-off from March's 2.2 and Italy's lowest reading for 28 years.
The month on month rate was 0.1 percent, the same as in March.
Bond futures brokers said there was talk in the markets of the possibility of lower rates in the next few days. "The short end of the market is bid on the back of it," one broker said.

The Bank of Italy on Monday let the minimum rate in its securities repurchase operations fall to 6.99 percent from 7.09 previously. This was the lowest level since 1982 and was read by some as a sign that a cut was on the way.

Analysts said while they could not rule out a rate cut in the next few days, it was unlikely the official CPI data would prod the central bank into easing directly because its priority for now was a strong, stable lira.
Francesco Giordano, Italian economist at Credit Suisse First Boston, said he did not expect an interest rate cut today but a 50 basis point one towards the end May was possible.
"I have a feeling the Bank of Italy wants a longer period of lira stability before cutting," Giordano said.

He thought the central bank wanted the lira firmer than its 990 per mark central parity in Europe's currency mechanism with a level of around 985 preferable. The lira underwent weakness in early April but is now stabilising near 990.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio began easing rates last July. With only two cuts since then, he has won the bank a reputation for toughness which he is keen to maintain.
Economists said Fazio could wait until preliminary May CPI data comes out around May 20, providing the lira is stable.

But the timing is hard to predict. Pio De Gregorio at NatWest Markets here said a 0.75 point cut was likely after Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government presents its document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF) by the end of May.

The central bank might also await French elections in late May and early June given that opposition socialists there, who are narrowing the government's lead in polls, want European economic and monetary union (EMU) under certain conditions.
"Clearly there is scope for easing in monetary policy but the Bank of Italy would prefer to wait for the government's budget plans and the French election results," De Gregorio said.
At Milan brokers Caboto, Chiara Manenti forecast a 50 basis point cut after the May preliminary CPI or in early June.
"The Bank of Italy's decision will be conditioned by external factors like the French elections and possible measures on the German deficit expected at the end of the month," she said.
Rodolfo Dozio at Banca Commerciale Italiana said the central bank's past behaviour on rates showed it also paid attention to the government's management of public finances.

Martino Dolfini at Chase Manhattan here, who expected a 75 basis point reduction by the end of May, noted: "The absence of cut in the last few weeks makes you understand the Bank of Italy doesn't exclusively follow an inflation objective."
